decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [250705-DWG-001 Rev A, 250705-DWG-002 Rev A, 250705-DWG-003 Rev A, 250705-DWG-005 Rev A, 250705-DWG-006 Rev A, Design and Access statement, Plant Noise Impact Assessment, Odour Appraisal, Fire statement received 09 August 2025].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 3 - The scheme of extract ventilation shown on the approved plans and specifications shall be carried out before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use and shall be maintained as specified thereafter and in accordance with the manufacturer's guidelines.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 4 - a) The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) to which this permission refers, shall be 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, at all times that the plant operate. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive premises or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive premises, and in accordance to the latest British Standard 4142. An alternative position for assessment/measurement may be used to allow ease of access, this must be shown on a map and noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria are achieved. 

b) The plant shall be isolated on adequate proprietary anti-vibration mounts to prevent the structural transmission of vibration and regenerated noise within adjacent or adjoining premises, and these shall be so maintained thereafter.   

c) Following installation of any mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) to which the application refers, a post completion noise assessment shall be submitted for approval to the local planning authority which demonstrates the actual measured rating level of plant operating under normal conditions. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the methodology of BS4142: 2014 (Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent amendments. The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review. If the plant fails to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again.  This shall be repeated until the assessment has reached the required standard.  Once achieved, the plant shall be maintained permanently ther

Condition : 5 - The use of the commercial kitchen extraction system shall not be permitted between the hours of 22:00 to 08:00 Mondays to Saturdays, nor between the hours of 22:00-09:00 on Sundays and Public/Bank Holidays. 
Reason: To ensure that the amenity of occupiers of the surrounding premises is not adversely affected by noise from operation of the kitchen extraction system.

Condition : 6 - Prior to commencement of the development, details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Council of a suitable cleaning schedule and/or maintenance contract for the extract and odour control system. Approved details shall be implemented prior to first operation of the system and thereafter be permanently retained. 
Reason: To ensure that the amenity of occupiers of the surrounding premises is not adversely affected by smell and odour.
